seo.title: NADRA Marriage Certificate: Process, Documents & Fees
seo.description: How to get your NADRA marriage certificate in Pakistan: Union Council registration, documents, fees and timelines. Get it right the first time.

hero.h1: NADRA Marriage Certificate in Pakistan: How to Get Your MRC, Documents, Fees and Timeline
hero.intro: A NADRA marriage certificate, officially the Marriage Registration Certificate (MRC), is the computerized government record of your marriage, issued by NADRA once your nikah is registered with the Union Council. You need it, not just your nikah nama, for a spouse visa, a passport update, or any official use of your marriage abroad. This guide covers registration, the NADRA application, documents, fees, and what to do if your nikah was never registered or the record now needs correcting.

howTo.name: How to Get a NADRA Marriage Certificate in Pakistan

steps.name: Register the nikah with the Union Council
steps.text: Confirm the nikah has been reported for registration to the Union Council where it was performed, as required under Section 5 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961. This is the nikah registrar's duty, but couples should verify it happened rather than assume it.

steps.name: Gather the required documents
steps.text: Collect the original registered nikah nama and a copy, CNICs of both spouses, the witnesses' details, photographs where required, and proof of any earlier marriage's end if applicable.

steps.name: Apply for the NADRA marriage certificate
steps.text: Either spouse applies through the Union Council, an e-Khidmat Markaz in Punjab, or the nearest NADRA Registration Centre, submitting the registered nikah nama and supporting documents.

steps.name: Complete biometric verification
steps.text: Expect fingerprint verification against your CNIC record at the counter as a standard part of processing the application.

steps.name: Collect and safeguard the certificate
steps.text: Once issued, keep the original MRC safe and get certified copies made for separate uses such as a passport office and a visa application, rather than sending the original abroad by post.

steps.name: Complete attestation if the MRC will be used abroad
steps.text: For use outside Pakistan, take the MRC through MOFA attestation and then either an Apostille or embassy attestation, depending on the destination country.

bodyMarkdown:
**By Bilal Saeed, Advocate (Punjab Bar Council), Lahore High Court and District Courts Lahore. Reviewed and last updated 10 August 2026.**

This article is general information about Pakistani marriage-registration procedure, not legal advice. Requirements, documents, and fees are set by NADRA and by each Union Council, and they change periodically. Confirm current requirements with your Union Council, e-Khidmat Markaz, or a lawyer before you apply.

A NADRA marriage certificate, more precisely called the Marriage Registration Certificate (MRC), is the computerized government record of your marriage. [NADRA](https://www.nadra.gov.pk) issues it once your nikah has been registered with the Union Council that has jurisdiction over where the marriage took place. You need the MRC, not just your nikah nama, for a spouse visa, a passport update after marriage, embassy attestation, or any official use of your marriage outside Pakistan. Most delays come from confusing the two documents, applying to the wrong Union Council, or a name that does not match CNIC records. This guide covers registration, the NADRA application, documents, fees, and what to do if the marriage was never registered or the record now needs correcting.

## Nikah nama vs NADRA marriage certificate: two different documents

The nikah nama and the NADRA marriage certificate are not the same document, and mixing them up is the single biggest cause of delay we see.

The **[nikah nama](/blog/nikah-nama-in-pakistan)** is the marriage contract itself: the document signed at the nikah by the bride, the groom, the two witnesses, and the nikah registrar. It records the dower (haq mehr) and any special conditions, and it is what most people mean when they say "shadi certificate."

The **NADRA marriage certificate (MRC)** is a separate, later step: the computerized government record NADRA generates after the nikah nama has been registered with the Union Council. It is not created automatically. Someone has to apply for it, using the registered nikah nama as the source document, and NADRA issues it in the standard format that embassies, passport offices, and immigration authorities recognize.

The practical difference:

- A nikah nama proves the marriage happened and states its terms.
- An MRC proves the marriage is registered in the national database, in a machine-readable, internationally recognized format.
- You cannot get an MRC without a registered nikah nama.
- A nikah nama alone is often not accepted for a spouse visa or a passport update. Most foreign missions want the NADRA-issued certificate.

If your nikah nama is years old and you never applied for the MRC, that is still fixable. You do not need to remarry. You apply for the MRC using the nikah nama you already have, though if the underlying nikah was never registered with the Union Council at all, that step has to happen first.

## Step 1: Register the nikah with the Union Council

Under Section 5 of the [Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961](https://pakistancode.gov.pk), every nikah in Pakistan must be reported for registration to the Union Council of the area where the nikah was performed. In practice, this duty falls on the nikah registrar who conducted the ceremony, but couples should confirm registration happened rather than assume it.

This is the Union Council marriage registration step, and everything downstream depends on it. The registrar records the nikah nama in the Union Council's register and issues its own attested copy. Skip this step and there is no official record for NADRA to draw on, so you cannot get an MRC.

**Which Union Council?** Jurisdiction generally follows the location where the nikah was solemnized, not where either party lives. If you married in Lahore but live elsewhere, the Lahore Union Council covering that address is usually the right one. [VERIFY WITH FIRM: exact jurisdiction rule where the nikah location and the parties' residence differ]

**What if the registrar didn't register it?** This happens more often than people expect, especially with hurried ceremonies, a private nikah khawan outside a formal setting, or nikahs conducted abroad. MFLO 1961 provides for a penalty where a registrar fails to report registration, though the exact amount and procedure are technical and best confirmed with a lawyer. Late registration is possible, but it typically means returning to the Union Council with the original nikah nama and, sometimes, the witnesses or an affidavit, rather than a routine same-day process.

This applies whatever route your nikah took, including a nikah performed at a court-marriage office rather than a mosque or family setting: registration with the Union Council is a separate step from the nikah itself.

## Step 2: Apply for the NADRA marriage certificate

Once the nikah is registered with the Union Council, either spouse can apply for the NADRA marriage certificate. In Punjab, most people do this through an e-Khidmat Markaz, the provincial one-window facilitation centre that handles NADRA and other government services alongside Union Council functions. Outside Punjab, or where no e-Khidmat Markaz is convenient, the application goes through the Union Council or the nearest NADRA Registration Centre.

**Who can apply.** Either the husband or the wife can submit the application. A representative can sometimes apply on a spouse's behalf with the right authorization, which matters for overseas Pakistanis who cannot travel back in person. [VERIFY WITH FIRM: current process for an overseas spouse applying without attending in person]

**What happens at application.** You submit the registered nikah nama (the Union Council-attested version, not a private copy), your CNIC, and the supporting documents listed below. Counter staff verify the nikah nama against the Union Council register, then forward the application into NADRA's system, which generates the computerized certificate. Expect biometric (fingerprint) verification against your CNIC record as a routine part of the process.

**Collecting the certificate.** Once issued, keep the original somewhere safe and get certified copies made if you need more than one, for example one for a passport office and one for a visa application, since sending an original abroad by post carries obvious risk.

This is the step most people mean when they ask how to get a NADRA marriage certificate: registration has to happen first, and the NADRA or e-Khidmat application is what produces the document you can actually use for a visa or passport update.

## Documents you will need

The exact checklist can vary slightly by Union Council or e-Khidmat Markaz, so treat this as the standard list rather than a guarantee. [VERIFY WITH FIRM: current, union-council-specific document checklist]

- **Original nikah nama**, plus a photocopy, showing Union Council registration, not just the nikah registrar's signature.
- **CNICs of both spouses**, originals for verification plus photocopies.
- **CNICs of the two nikah witnesses**, where the Union Council asks for them, or the witnesses' details as recorded on the nikah nama.
- **Passport-size photographs** of the applicant, and sometimes of both spouses, depending on the centre.
- **CNIC of the applicant** submitting the request, if different from one of the spouses, for example a close relative applying with authorization.
- For a **[second or subsequent marriage](/blog/second-marriage-law-in-pakistan)**: proof relating to the earlier marriage's status ([divorce certificate](/blog/divorce-procedure-in-pakistan), [khula order](/blog/khula-procedure-in-pakistan), or death certificate of a deceased former spouse), since NADRA and the Union Council record marital history.
- For an **overseas applicant**: a valid passport and, in some cases, an authorization letter for whoever is applying in Pakistan on their behalf.

Bring originals even when the counter only keeps photocopies. Union Council and NADRA staff routinely ask to see the original nikah nama and CNICs before accepting copies, and turning up without them is one of the most common reasons people have to make a second trip.

## Fees and how long it takes

NADRA and Union Council services generally offer a normal-processing fee and a higher urgent fee for faster turnaround, similar to CNIC and other NADRA services. The exact rupee amounts are not figures we can quote here: they are set by NADRA and the provincial e-Khidmat schedule, and they are revised from time to time. [VERIFY WITH FIRM: current MRC fee schedule the firm quotes clients] Check the fee posted at your e-Khidmat Markaz or Union Council counter on the day rather than relying on a number quoted elsewhere, and be cautious of anyone quoting a fee well above what the counter charges.

Processing time follows a similar pattern: a standard track and a faster, more expensive urgent track, and the difference between them matters if you are working against a visa interview or passport appointment. [VERIFY WITH FIRM: current standard and urgent processing timelines quoted to clients]

The most reliable way to protect a deadline is to start early. If your nikah was never registered, that step has to happen before NADRA can issue anything, and it is not something rushed through in a single visit if witnesses or an affidavit are needed. Build in a buffer, especially if the marriage is old, unregistered, or involves a name discrepancy that needs sorting out first.

## If you had a court marriage

A court marriage is not a different kind of marriage in Pakistani law. It is a nikah, performed and documented at a Union Council or Family Court setting rather than in a home or mosque, but the same MFLO 1961 rules apply. See our full guide to [court marriage in Pakistan](/blog/court-marriage-in-pakistan) if you are earlier in that process.

Where couples get tripped up is assuming that because a court marriage happens at or near the Union Council, registration is automatic. It is not. The nikah still has to be formally registered by the nikah registrar, and the MRC still has to be separately applied for through NADRA or e-Khidmat afterward. A court marriage solemnized but never followed through to registration leaves you in the same position as an unregistered mosque nikah: no MRC until the registration gap is closed.

This comes up often with couples who married quickly, sometimes against family wishes, and treated the Union Council paperwork as finished once the nikah nama was signed. The fix is usually straightforward: go back to the same Union Council, confirm whether it was in fact registered (sometimes it was, and the couple simply never collected the MRC), and if not, complete registration before applying for the certificate. A family dispute or protection order connected to the marriage is a separate legal matter, worth raising alongside the paperwork.

## Using the MRC abroad: attestation chain

A NADRA marriage certificate on its own is not always enough for use outside Pakistan. Most embassies, immigration authorities, and foreign registries want it attested through Pakistan's standard document chain before they will accept it.

For a marriage certificate, that chain generally runs from NADRA, as the issuing authority for the computerized MRC, through to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Our full guide on [MOFA attestation in Pakistan](/blog/mofa-attestation-in-pakistan) sets out the complete chain, including the prior-authority step, the MOFA appointment process, and the final step for your destination country.

**Apostille or embassy attestation.** After MOFA, the last step depends on where the certificate is going. Since Pakistan joined the [Hague Apostille Convention](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/specialised-sections/apostille), many member countries accept a single Apostille in place of full embassy legalisation. For countries outside the Convention, embassy or high-commission attestation is still the route. Which one applies is decided by the destination country, not by you, so check the receiving authority's own requirements before you start.

**English or Urdu.** The MRC issued by NADRA is in a standard bilingual computerized format. Most receiving authorities accept this as-is; some ask for a certified translation on top of attestation. [VERIFY WITH FIRM: which destination countries or visa categories currently ask for a translated MRC alongside attestation]

**Spouse visa use.** For a [spouse or family visa](/immigration-lawyer-in-lahore), the MRC is usually the core document proving the marriage, alongside the nikah nama and any joint evidence the receiving country asks for. Applying well before you need to submit avoids a last-minute scramble through both registration and attestation at once.

## Common problems and how a lawyer fixes them

Most of what we see in this area is not dramatic. It is small procedural snags that stall an application at the counter.

**Name or spelling mismatch.** The name on the nikah nama does not match the CNIC exactly, whether a transliteration difference, a missing middle name, or a father's name recorded differently, and NADRA will often refuse to issue the MRC until this is resolved. Example (illustrative): a client's nikah nama and CNIC used slightly different transliterations of the same name. NADRA held the application until the discrepancy was corrected through a supporting affidavit and the Union Council record was reconciled. This is fixable, but it needs the right document, not a second attempt at the same counter.

**Unregistered old nikah.** Couples married years, sometimes decades, ago who never registered with the Union Council at the time. Late registration is possible under the MFLO framework, but it is not a routine over-the-counter process once significant time has passed, and it usually needs the original nikah nama, the witnesses if available, and sometimes a supporting affidavit.

**Lost nikah nama.** Without the original registered nikah nama, there is no source document for NADRA to work from. The first step is checking whether the Union Council still holds its own copy in the register, since the copy given to the couple is not the only record. Example (illustrative): a couple who lost their nikah nama in a house move assumed they would have to start over. Their original Union Council still had it on file, and a certified copy from that register was enough to move the NADRA application forward.

**Registrar refusal or delay.** Occasionally a Union Council refuses or delays registration, sometimes over a jurisdiction dispute, sometimes over an incomplete file. A written application, or where necessary a formal legal request, moves this along faster than repeat visits.

**Correcting the record after issuance.** If the MRC itself is issued with an error, whether a name, a date, or a witness detail, there is a correction process through NADRA and the Union Council rather than a fresh application from zero.

In each of these, the practical value of a lawyer is knowing which document clears the specific hold, rather than resubmitting the same file and hoping.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the difference between a nikah nama and a NADRA marriage certificate?**

The nikah nama is the marriage contract signed at the nikah itself, recording the dower and terms agreed by both parties. The NADRA marriage certificate (MRC) is a separate, later document: the computerized government record NADRA issues once that nikah nama has been registered with the Union Council. You need the registered nikah nama before NADRA can issue an MRC.

**How can I get a NADRA marriage certificate?**

First, make sure your nikah is registered with the Union Council where it was performed, which is the nikah registrar's legal duty under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961. Then either spouse applies for the MRC through the Union Council, an e-Khidmat Markaz in Punjab, or the nearest NADRA Registration Centre, submitting the registered nikah nama and CNICs.

**What documents are required for a NADRA marriage certificate?**

You generally need the original registered nikah nama and a photocopy, CNICs of both spouses, and the witnesses' CNICs or details as recorded on the nikah nama, plus photographs where the centre asks for them. If either spouse was previously married, proof of that marriage's end (divorce or death certificate) is also needed. The exact checklist varies by Union Council.

**How much does a NADRA marriage certificate cost?**

There is generally a normal-processing fee and a higher urgent fee, similar to other NADRA services, but exact rupee amounts are set by NADRA and the provincial e-Khidmat schedule and change periodically. Check the fee posted at your Union Council or e-Khidmat Markaz counter on the day rather than relying on a figure quoted elsewhere.

**Can I get an MRC if my nikah was never registered?**

Yes, but registration has to happen first. The Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 provides for late registration of an unregistered nikah, though it is not a routine same-day process once significant time has passed. You typically need the original nikah nama and, depending on the Union Council, the witnesses or a supporting affidavit before NADRA can issue the certificate.

**Can overseas Pakistanis apply for a marriage certificate?**

Yes. The underlying nikah still needs to be registered with the relevant Union Council in Pakistan, but the MRC application can sometimes be handled by an authorized representative or family member on the applicant's behalf. Requirements for applying without attending in person vary, so confirm the current process with the Union Council or a lawyer before relying on it.

**Is the NADRA marriage certificate valid for spouse visa applications?**

Yes, the MRC is generally the core document foreign missions want as proof of marriage for a spouse or family visa, alongside the nikah nama. Many destination countries also require it to go through Pakistan's attestation chain, MOFA then Apostille or embassy attestation, before they accept it, so check the receiving country's specific requirements before you apply.
